title: SCA Minhag of the Week 295: “The 1897 Printing of the Haggadah in Aleppo”

chapters.title: The 1897 Aleppo Haggadah
chapters.about: Introduction to the 1897 printing in Halab and its 2004 reproduction.

chapters.title: Textual Wording and Kehach Ma'anya
chapters.about: Comparison of Halach Ma'anya and Kehach Ma'anya in various Haggadot.

chapters.title: Arabic Translation and Avadim Hayinu
chapters.about: Discussion of Hadal Jawad and traditional pronunciation.

chapters.title: Pronunciation and Specific Paragraphs
chapters.about: Shacharit, Lish'ol, Afikomin, and Baruch Shomer Haftahato.

chapters.title: Mishadotam and Conclusion
chapters.about: Omission of Mishadotam and preservation of community customs.

summary: Joey Harari examines the 1897 printing of the Haggadah in Halab and compares its text and pronunciation to other editions. He discusses specific wording differences, Arabic translations, and traditional customs preserved in community Haggadot.
questions: What is significant about the 1897 Haggadah printed in Halab?
How does the 1897 Aleppo Haggadah spell and pronounce certain key phrases like Kehach Ma'anya?
Why does the Haggadah use Lish'ol instead of Lesh'ol for the son who does not know how to ask?
What Arabic addition is sung before Avadim Hayinu according to community custom?
